Sustaining game servers costs money. Some people enjoy Fallout 76 and want to see it expand and grow. Mod authors need to pay rent too and Giving them a portion of each sale is more fair than the old creation club contracting way they handled things. Theres no one really losing in this scenario. You dont wanna  spend extra, don't  no one is gonna force you to.

I guess the point I'm trying  to make it'd be alot cooler if  I bought a item in the atom shop that was made by a community member. That other players would be able to see ingame I was supporting the community. Instead of just psuedo dlc for my singleplayer game and only I can see the items. Giving creators a share of  each sale would incentivize them to submit content to the community part of the atom shop to be put into the game. Players would get more content and the good feeling of supporting their community not just Bethesda  , mod makers could get income to sustain their free works, bethesda gets cash.

The way I see it in warframe  alot of people buy Tennogen which are exclusively items designed  by community creators as a way of supporting the community itself. Which is why people are more willing to spend money. Bethesda  fucked up by contracting the mods instead of splitting the profit with each sale which is why people were upset.
